HediffDef.label: vital resistance therapy
HediffDef.description: Active for about five days. This experimental treatment strongly disrupts Wraith life-force extraction but does not make the pawn immune to feeding attempts. A treated victim suffers much less extraction; a rejected attempt can instead trigger a temporary life-force rejection crisis in the victim and a short feeding-link backlash in the Wraith. The treatment is therefore protection with a cost, not a harmless hard counter.

HediffDef.label: resistance-treatment strain
HediffDef.description: The anti-feeding treatment is forcing the body to maintain an unnatural metabolic rejection state. For roughly one to one-and-a-half days after treatment, movement, manipulation and consciousness are mildly reduced. This is the immediate physiological price of gaining strong temporary feeding resistance.

HediffDef.label: life-force rejection crisis
HediffDef.description: A Wraith feeding attempt collided with the pawn's active vital resistance therapy. Life-force extraction was greatly reduced, but the violent metabolic rejection temporarily destabilises movement, manipulation and consciousness. The resistance worked; this crisis is the cost of forcing the feeding link to fail.

HediffDef.label: feeding rejection backlash
HediffDef.description: The Wraith's feeding link was violently rejected by a victim under active vital resistance therapy. For several hours the psychic and metabolic recoil reduces awareness, sight and fine control. This is the Wraith-side consequence of attempting to feed through a treated victim.
